newsitem.title: USA: Heavy snow slows livestock movement in U.S. Plains.
newsitem.headline: Heavy snow slows livestock movement in U.S. Plains.

text.p: Heavy snow hampered livestock movement in South Dakota and portions of Nebraska and Iowa on Tuesday and storms were expected to push east across the U.S. Midwest later in the day, meteorologists said.
"It looks like they had another five to 10 inches of snow across South Dakota, northern Nebraska and northwest Iowa in the past 24 hours," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
The storm system was pushing east across Illinois and Indiana Tuesday morning with rain expected to change to snow as temperatures dropped.
Light snow was forecast for northern Illinois and Indiana with the heaviest accumulations in the northern Great Lakes region.
Colder air follows behind the storm system but temperatures were not expected to be significantly colder, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.
"Temperatures behind the system are not excessively cold with readings this morning in the single digits to teens (degrees Fahrenheit) in the western Dakotas," Gesser said.
Lows Wednesday morning should be near zero F in the central Midwest, he said.
